drivers.detail: 'One of the biggest factors in order cost'
cost rises with number of laser pierces; 40 holes cheaper than 100
intricate patterns, perforations, thin bridges take longer; no $/length rate published
material used and machine time; keep largest dimension < 28 in to keep cost low
discounts start at 2 identical parts, per line item only; '50 of the same part can give you a 50% discount'; bulk 'up to 80%'
each service adds cost; quantity discounts also apply to services; bent parts have a minimum charge
pre-nested files cost more; upload one part per file

minimum_order.note: SendCutSend: no minimum quantity on most processes. Free US shipping at >= $39 (US and Canada only). OSH Cut's self-published comparison claims a '$39 minimum' for SendCutSend - conflicts with SendCutSend's own pages; treat $39 as the free-shipping threshold.

lead_times.fastest: within 24 h (rush + overnight + order by noon PT)

quoting_access.api_note: No public API documented (sendcutsend.com/api and /developers return 404). Instant quote = upload DXF/DWG/AI/EPS/STEP at sendcutsend.com. CAD plug-ins: Autodesk Fusion and SolidWorks (live quotes + cart). An unauthenticated JSON of material specs exists at app.sendcutsend.com/materials (used by their bending calculator) - undocumented, may change; use for rules, not prices.

derived_estimates.label: ESTIMATE derived by us from the published examples above - not a SendCutSend rate

pricing_model.estimate_formula_note: SendCutSend does not publish its formula. For the designer use: price_each(qty) ~= max(bbox_in2 * rate_qty1[material], floor) * qty_factor(qty) + services, with rate_qty1 ~ $1.0-1.1/in2 of bounding box for small simple 5052 parts and ~$4.9/in2 for 1 mm CF (both ESTIMATES from 2-3 examples), qty_factor(100) ~ 0.21-0.55 (median 0.31 across 15 published examples), and a bent-part minimum (~$19 implied). Always label results 'estimate - confirm by uploading the DXF'. Prices follow commodity costs.

material_ladder.basis: Bambu Lab TDS values (XY flexural modulus/strength, Z tensile, HDT at 1.8 MPa) relative to PLA Basic; price = $/kg (refill where sold) on 2026-10-25

formulas.governing: use the larger of the two factors; also check Z (layer) strength if load crosses layers

material_ladder.label: DERIVED from published TDS values with standard beam theory (not vendor data)
material_ladder.caveat: TDS specimens are 100% infill, annealed/dried; real parts with walls+infill are weaker. Bambu PETG Basic has LOWER flexural modulus than PLA Basic (1.95 vs 2.75 GPa) - PETG parts must be ~12% thicker for equal stiffness.

orientation.flat_vs_upright_pla: 63 MPa flat vs 31 MPa upright (~50%); 45 deg gives 40 MPa (+27% vs upright)
orientation.rule: Lay leg links flat so bending stresses run along layers; CF-filled filaments are much more anisotropic (Z/XY ~0.34-0.47) than plain PLA (~0.89).

walls_vs_infill.finding: bending/torsion load is carried at the outer skin; gradient (outer-dense) infill was ~30% stiffer at equal weight; 100% infill gave 43,406 cycles vs 28,325 at 50% in tension-tension fatigue and E 2553 vs 2004 MPa
walls_vs_infill.rule: For leg links: many walls (perimeters filling the outer region) + high infill near bolt holes; wall count number not published by a cited source - choose by test.

fatigue_and_static_allowables_pla.rule: Design PLA legs to <= 22 MPa peak static stress and <= 10% of TDS UTS for cyclic (stance/landing) stress: PLA Basic 35 MPa XY -> 3.5 MPa cyclic (derived).

heat.pla_softening: PLA Basic HDT 54 C @1.8 MPa, Vicat 57 C, Tg 60 C (TDS); CNC Kitchen loaded oven test: PLA gives at 60 C, PETG 80 C, ASA 110 C
heat.rule: Any printed part touching a motor stator/housing: not PLA unless measured housing temp stays well below 54 C. Options on a P1S: PETG (HDT 68), ASA (92), annealed HT-PLA Pro (107.6 @0.45 MPa). Motor temperatures were not researched here.

annealing_pla.result: 100 C / 45 min: tensile +7.5%, hook +16%, but up to 10% shrink in XY and growth in Z; not correctable by scaling

pla_plus.result: PolyMax PLA+ vs PolyLite PLA: 43 vs 57 MPa tensile, ~2200 vs ~3000 MPa stiffness, ~4x impact, same 65 C heat failure

creep.pla_note: no vendor creep data published; design to the static reference above and test bolted joints
creep.pa6_cf: un-annealed PA6-CF bolted joint needed re-tightening almost daily for a week; annealing 8 h at 110 C brought creep close to other polymers; PA12-CF needed one re-tightening

nylon_moisture.result: conditioned PA6-CF (~3% water) kept 56% of dry strength and ~1/3 of stiffness; PA12-CF lost ~15% strength; dry 80 C ~20 h

hole_and_bearing_seat_fit.rule: Calibrate with a test coupon using the same filament/profile; correct with Bambu Studio XY hole compensation (holes only) and XY contour compensation (outer size). No numeric press-fit allowance published by Bambu.

nozzle_rules.rule: CF/GF filled filaments need a hardened steel nozzle; 0.6 mm first choice (0.4 hardened OK for Bambu PLA-CF/PETG-CF); never 0.2 mm; stainless/brass wear quickly. P1S stainless nozzle was visibly worn after 10 h of PETG-CF.

enclosure_rules.rule: PA/PC/ABS/ASA and their CF/GF variants need an enclosed printer; PLA/PETG/TPU fine open-frame (enclosure recommended for PETG). With PLA in an enclosed printer and bed > 45 C, open the door/remove the top glass. PPS-CF only on H2 series and X1E.

tpu_tyres.rule: TPU 85A/90A/95A HF are not AMS-compatible (feed spool directly); 'TPU for AMS' is 68D and much stiffer (1.19 GPa) - for bumpers, not grippy tyres. TPU 95A HF: 27.3 MPa, >650% elongation.

fasteners_notes: Pivots: hobby five-bar legs (Stanford Doggo) stack two deep-groove bearings in one link and run a shoulder bolt through them into the opposing link; drive links use a drilled/tapped set-screw hole (https://github.com/Nate711/StanfordDoggoProject). Shoulder bolts: VXB 20-pack M6x1.0 thread / 8 mm shoulder x 12 mm, $49.98 (~$2.50 each) (https://vxb.com/products/20-pack-shoulder-bolts-m6-10-x-12-mm-thread-8-mm-d); McMaster/Misumi prices not retrieved. Heat-set inserts (CNC Kitchen store, 2026-10-25): M3x5.7 100 pcs $9.40, M4x8.1 50 pcs $9.90, M5x9.5 50 pcs $9.90, M3/M4/M5 200-pc set $25.90 (https://cnckitchen.store). M3 insert pull-out ~1400 N in PLA; torque-out 3 Nm vs 1 Nm for a screw straight into PETG; bottom-pocket captive nut gave the highest pull-out (166 kg) in PETG. CF tubes cannot be threaded (Easy Composites); join with bonded inserts/clamps. 3M DP420 is the usual structural epoxy for tube-to-insert bonds but its TDS could not be fetched (3M blocks automated access) - strength values null. SendCutSend can tap M2-M16 and press PEM nuts/standoffs/studs into aluminium from .040 in.
